utterances.text: That is according to you. Not according to me. In my view, it was just a matter of when somebody is afraid and they are suffering from something, then they are afraid for themselves and not -- they are afraid of you or of me. So it gets a little bit complicated. But all of those medical certificates were objectively written according to the history of the illness pursuant to the information provided to me by -- provided by the patient on the basis of the medical examination by the doctor. It seems as if it were false because people may consider it to be that way, but these are not false certificates.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, you are very clear here. You say yourself in your statement that the the permits were false. I'm quoting you. So, Mr. Sabanovic --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: -- did the military authorities warn you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: The officers from Banja Luka came from the military court. I don't know if they were actually from the military court, but I think that they were. They came to see me, and the issuance continued for as many as people who were there who needed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, you say in your statement: "In spite of their instructions, I continued to issue those permits."

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not in spite of them. They said hello to me, and then they left nicely. I just said, I do have the right to issue these medical permits.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, then when you were issuing those several thousand, you said you continued to do that, so several thousand permits. The evasion of military duty was a serious violation subject to a substantial prison sentence. Let me just ask you, by this activity of yours, did you assist such a large number of people to commit such a serious criminal act?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: None of those people committed a criminal act. These were people who felt unfit - falsely, according to you - but this was not a crime. I would be getting into trouble for lesser things than the ones that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: But you did not suffer particularly because you issued these false permits?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: These were not false permits. These were issued to people who were unfit for combat between those two states.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In such a large number?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, such a large number. That was in accordance to the number of the population in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I served in the military, so the number of those unfit according to some percentages could not have been more than a few dozen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not admit that they are false. I did say that I issued them but this is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution made a mistake when they were taking your statement?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I said on a number of times --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm sorry to intervene, but the interpreters are having difficulty. Question, answer. Please wait for the interval to allow the interpreters to catch up.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honours. May I continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, now I'm going to be open. You were a member of the party of democratic action and with this activity of yours did you implement the policy of the SDA and the HDZ, which consisted of, amongst other things, of toppling the Yugoslav People's Army as an institution of federal significance entrusted with preserving the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: This is so dangerous what you are saying, so I really don't know where are you getting this force from, for me to include the health aspect into the policy of the SDA or the HDZ. That was your tactic right from the beginning, and that is why you brought about the situation, to see who suffered in this war, which you cannot even describe as a war because the place where I live there --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, could you please reply with a yes or no. Did you include this in the policy of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing was like that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking if you repeat the question. Again counsel and witness have slipped into the habit of overlapping the questions and the answers. Please bear in mind the work of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please put this document on the ELMO now. 1D00-3848.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, I assume that you cannot see what this looks like. This document on the left-hand side, the copy is a little bit bad.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: What would you like me to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you the decision, and then we'll comment on it. This is a small municipality of Citluk. You will agree that the municipality of Citluk is a small municipality?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I was never there, but I assume that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And they reached a decision there about the moratorium on sending recruits to the JNA on the 19th of July, 1991, as early as that. So imagine, now, the situation where a small municipality like that in July 1991 introduces a moratorium on the sending of recruits to the JNA. That municipality was under the control of the HDZ. Now, I have to repeat the question which I owe due to the -- for the interpreters, and I'm asking you, did you join, by issuing these medical certificates, to the implementation of such a policy?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the first time that I'm hearing this now about me seeing, hearing, or joining any kind of endeavour like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Mr. Sabanovic, in your statement to the Prosecutor, you spoke about your arrest and you said, among other things, that when you were arrested, you were pushed into a military vehicle. Today, in response to a question by the Prosecutor, you said that it was a police vehicle. So what is correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: What is correct is that it was the police, the police. These were military policemen. That is the truth. I don't remember the vehicles. If I were able to do that after all these years, then I would be able to write whatever I -- I don't have any comments. I can't even listen to these lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: No, no, you have to be patient so we can clarify these things. So you were arrested by the military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read from your statement where you say: "I stayed for three days in the garage. Military -- Serbian military police offered us food. Most members of the military police were from Sanski Most." Is this true?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, there were both kinds. The military police were from Sana and from another place. It was the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Just be patient, just be patient. You have you have to wait for my question. In the next passage it says military guards would come occasionally to the garage at 0 -- 2000 hours, take me in front of the garage, and proceed to beat me; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Then you continue to talk about going to, I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the gym; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Counsel, there's an objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm trying to find this in the English transcript. I'd appreciate a page and line number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SAVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] This is the witness statement -- the interview from February 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, you were in the sports hall for a while; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Who was guarding the sports facility?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Who, which police?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean which police? You are asking me to be a professional, to be able to tell you what sort of a police. It was professional police, military police. As long as they were in Sana, every policemen had weapons, and they would come to this hall. Even civilians would enter this hall, look around, and beat whoever they wanted to. As for the police, it was the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you please wait for the interpreters to finish. Is it your final answer that it was the military police?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: It was the military police of the military. I don't know if it was a regular soldier or a military soldier. I don't know, I wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now look at exhibit from 65 ter list 611. Can we please look at page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you read what it says on the left-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we open the next page of that document, please. I apologise. Yes, this is only the interpreter's affirmation, so we need to look at the next page. This is it. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, as you can see, this is an order of the municipal staff of -- for civilian protection about the accommodation of refugees who withdrew from certain settlements to the sports hall. And then under paragraph Roman II, it says that military police of the Territorial Defence staff would be guarding the column. Does this confirm what you said about it being the military police that was involved?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: You would like me to be a military strategist?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Is that the answer to your question?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I forgot to ask that the previous document be tendered into evidence, and this is document 1D00-3848. And now I would like to have admitted this document that I have just shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I believe that the previous document that you showed, that is to say, 1D00-3848, the moratorium by the municipality in Citluk, the witness had no knowledge of this moratorium, he couldn't comment on it, he had never seen it before. I don't think it's appropriate to have this admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you have made this decision, and I am going to abide by it. I withdraw this document. But in the next document you can see what sort of police guarded the sports facility, and the witness is talking about that specifically. So I would ask for that document to be tendered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's one thing the sports hall where the population was brought and another thing is the gym --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sabanovic, I don't have a lot of time, so you will just permit me to put questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We are advised that the current document is already marked as an exhibit. It's already entered as an exhibit. Sorry, Anna, what is the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P60.8, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise if that slipped past me. I will just continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, you talked about going to Manjaca, and you say, among other things, that the following day, on the 3rd or the 4th of June, the military police arrived and ordered everyone to leave the sports facility. Is this correct what it says in your statement?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand you at all. I never said that, and something like that could not have come out of my mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm stating -- I'm reading your statement to the Prosecution which you signed.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: This cannot be. The commander of the whole --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. You said that you didn't say that, so I cannot force you. Mr. Sabanovic --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: All lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We are going to come to Manjaca. Can you please tell me who was there waiting for you when you got to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: The police, military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read a part of your statement where you say: "We were greeted by a lieutenant of the JNA, whose name I don't know, and soldiers." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. For me a military policemen is a soldier. As for this one, there was a corporal --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. You answered the question. Do you agree with this part of the statement where you say that you were greeted by a lieutenant of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was not the lieutenant. It was the military and the military police. But this was a man who I was not allowed to turn around. I heard him mention my name. He was the son of a chief --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You answered the question, Witness. I have to interrupt you because I have to continue to work with you so --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: You seem to know things better than I do. You were never there, but you seem to know things better than I do. Just one lie after another.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You said in your statement that representatives of international humanitarian organisations came, journalists and so on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at document from the 65 ter list 503.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, you can see from this document that the visit was approved by the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: They approved everything that they wished to approve.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Who was the commander of that corps; do you know?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Banja Luka Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You said today that General Talic would come to visit. What was the name of the commander of the camp?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Popovic. Bogdan Popovic. I think it was Bogdan Popovic. Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You just answered about his rank, so he was a lieutenant-colonel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that he enjoyed the trust of General Talic?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: According to the conversation, I was in contact every day and talked and Popovic would boast that he was held in high esteem by General Talic and that he could do whatever he wished as far as his work was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I apologise, Your Honours, I'm talking about this approval for the visit of the international commission. I would like to ask you to admit that and to give it an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D12, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In your statement you say that in conversation with some military policemen you concluded that Popovic enjoyed the trust of General Talic?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: In my discussions with the policemen and with Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Then in your statement you also say that the military policemen in the camp worked in shifts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I was not their supervisor. I wasn't asked to make any shifts and who would work when. I worked in the health centre in Sanski Most. I had nothing to do with the police. This is absurd.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, I'm merely quoting your statement.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Quote whatever you want, it's a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, please try to be quiet when I'm speaking, and I'm being warned all the time of the same. I'm merely quoting your statement in which you say that the MPs in the camp worked in shifts. Tell me something about the supply of water in the camp.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: First, there was a fountain in the stable where I was, for the cattle. Later on, some 3- to 500 people had to line up, use their tin cans to go down to the lake to bring water.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did the army do anything in order to reconstruct the pipeline, the water-pipe?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: We were told that such an attempt was made, but nothing of the sort was ever done.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show 1D00-4511.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, we now go back to the command of the 1st Krajina Corps. As you can see, it says that the water-supply system should be reconstructed because of the dissatisfactory bacteriological test results. You said that you knew of such reconstruction that was to take place.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard about that because I was with the police all the time as well as with the commander. I was in contact with them on a daily basis, but it never worked. I only know that the army brought in tank trucks with water to be used for showers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you heard of something like this planned, but nothing was done, in your words?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't done.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I thought the witness says that he didn't know of this. Could you assist me?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite the contrary, Your Honour. The witness said that he was familiar of the plans for reconstruction, but allegedly it never took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D13, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the next document to the witness, which is 1D00-5 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 4507.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: There, Mr. Sabanovic, be patient please, I'll put the question. The previous document was dated the 27th of July. And indeed on the 5th of August, 1992, the command is again urging to have the reconstruction done as in the interim as you yourself said was not. After this second intervention, was anything done with the water-supply system?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing was done. They were urging, as you put it, but nothing happened either the first or the second time around. The water was being brought in in cans from the lake for drinking, and tank trucks brought water for showers.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These documents are related, Your Honours, hence I seek to tender this one since it is directly related to the previous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D14, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, could you just clarify with the witness whether the water brought in the tanks was water that could be -- that you could drink or was it only for showers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not for drinking. It was for showering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Because it was contaminated or unclean water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I never did any tests. I only know that it was not supposed to be drank. It was for showers. And perhaps a truck was used to shower some 500 people. They will just sprinkle it over you and there you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, were any prisoners taken out of the camp to undertake some work while you were there?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show Defence exhibits relating to this. This is 1D00-4503.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, we, again, go back to the command of the 1st Krajina Corps. That command is addressing the camp management asking for 20 prisoners to carry out work in the period of ten days. Did those people indeed leave?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They cut wood, worked in the fields sewing corn, did other types of work depending on the season. They constructed the church. They did whatever was necessary and ordered in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Sabanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of them, a Catholic was even killed while working there cutting down timber.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the witness confirmed this, I would kindly ask that this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D15, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the next document is 1D00-4505.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, we won't dwell on this one too much. But here we see that 170 prisoners were supposed to be used for work on orders of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe the witness has already commented on this fact, and I would kindly ask that since it is related to the previous documents, this document be admitted as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was you and the command that were counting, although incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, the document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I apologise, Your Honour, for this oversight.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D16, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, who commanded the military police and the guards in Manjaca camp?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: The commander, the commander of the camp, and the warden of the camp who was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, were any people coming from the military security service to conduct interrogations of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: There were interrogators there who conducted interrogations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we show the next document to the witness. It is from the 65 ter list, number 655.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, please have a look at the document. It is the 1 1st Krajina Corps command, Department For Intelligence and Security Affairs. 2 In the document, it is stated that after processing, they carried out a 3 selection of prisoners and that some may be released as it was determined that 4 there was no reason to hold them any longer. You are not mentioned in the 5 document per se, but the citizens–the inhabitants of Sanski Most municipality. 6 It was signed by Colonel Stevan Bogajevic. Does this confirm the fact you 7 mentioned, namely that there were investigators who came in the camp? They say 8 here that they made a selection and some could be released home. 9 A. If this is the Bogojevic from the Banja Luka football club Borac, then he 10 was at Manjaca. 11 Q. I asked you to confirm this fact which I believe you did. Therefore, your 12 honours, I think that the document can be admitted, as the investigators from 13 the department... 14 A. Only one of them was there at the time... 15 MR. CVIJETIC:...for intelligence and security affairs indeed visited Manjaca. 16 Since the witness confirms that, I kindly seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D17, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, my last question in this cross-examination is, When did you hear for the first time in your life that there was someone called Mico Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: In that period. I don't know when. In the war period. Actually, in the post-war period.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you didn't hear of him during the war, but afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel, we are wondering whether it would be convenient to take the break now rather than interrupting your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, it's up to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can go on all night long, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... now, Your Honour. Go to the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was wondering if we could raise a scheduling matter concerning Ms. Hanson, at your convenience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, let's finish the witness and we can take this -- let's finish the witness and then there should be time to deal with administrative matters towards the end of the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, you may begin your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon Mr. Sabanovic. I am Dragan Krgovic. I'm Defence attorney for Stojan Zupljanin. I'm going to put some questions to you relating to mostly your testimony of today. I'm going to try to formulate my questions so that you can very simply respond with a yes or no. And if any clarification is necessary, you can also do that. I am going to give you time for that. In order to avoid overlapping, I would like to ask you to wait with your answer until there's been a little break. We speak the same language, and if in the transcript there's overlapping then it's difficult to have a record in the transcript of exactly what you said and then later that would require correction. So can you please observe this suggestion when you are giving your answers. Of course, this also applies to me because I also have the same problem. Mr. Sabanovic, in relation to your stay in Manjaca and everything that happened to you, you provided several statements. I even think you testified here in the Brdjanin case before this Tribunal; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When I'm talking about the statements, I'm talking about the statement you gave to the investigative organs in Germany, and also the statement you provided to the Prosecutor. That is what I will be referring to, these two statements. One that was given in 1999 on the 26th of May, that was given in Germany. And the second one is the statement given to the investigators from the Prosecutor's Office of the 1st and 2nd of December; and the 14th and the 17th of February; and the 19th of February, 1991 [as interpreted]. Do you agree that these are these two statements?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And since a lot of time has passed since those events, almost 17 years, and it's normal, like you said today, that you do not recall every single detail, and it's possible that even if you tried your best, you still wouldn't be able to remember every detail; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, I think there might be a mistake in the transcript, page 62, line 24 reads statement dated the 19th of February, 1991. Perhaps my friend can clarify that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said, and the witness confirmed that it was 2001. I apologise. Well, probably the interpreters didn't hear me correctly. I'm talking about the statement you gave to the Prosecutor; we are talking about the 2001, after all of these events. And in the transcript it was entered wrongly that you provided statements in 1991, so this is all I wanted to say. This is the essence of the intervention by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me that the statement that you gave immediately after these events reflect what you said according to your best recollection and your recollection at the time was the best in relation to these events; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: A lot of time has passed since then, now even more time has passed, so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But, of course, you remembered better nine or ten years ago what happened than you do now; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, I'm going to show you the statement you gave to the Prosecutor, and I would like you to confirm whether we are talking about the same statement in order to avoid any misunderstandings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness his statement in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, could you please look at the statement that is in the B/C/S, as they call it here. It's the Bosnian, Croatian, and Serbian. This is how we refer to our language here in the Tribunal. Is it your signature on that statement?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, this is not my signature. This is not my signature. This is my signature at the top, but not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's not all your signature, one is your signature and the second signature is by the person who took the statement and who also translated. Can you please repeat what you said loudly, that one is your signature and the other is the signature of another person?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. What should I do now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to put some questions to you. Please, you, when you testified in the Brdjanin case, and in this statement mention different persons who came to visit the military prison or camp in Manjaca. In the statement, please, can you look at this version in our language. This is on page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The same version in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you found page 16? The number is at the bottom of the page, perhaps it's not so easy to find.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and what am I supposed to do now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at paragraph 5 from the top. Take your glasses, please. The paragraph begins with these words: "Slobodan" [as interpreted] "Zupljanin came to the camp..."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are unable to see where he is reading.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, but the transcript reads: "Slobodan Zupljanin came to the camp ..." And I think that was an error.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stojan Zupljanin, it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I looked at that. This is the last sentence of that paragraph, and it says: "That is the only occasion in which I know for sure that Stojan Zupljanin visited the camp."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This is at the bottom of page 15 and the top of page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So, very well. The last sentence in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember ever saying that to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably. Probably. Because I heard that he had come on another occasion, but I wasn't there. Perhaps this is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You testified in the Brdjanin case after you provided this statement?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Then you testified for three days and the Prosecutor also asked you then who had come to Manjaca, and amongst others - this is page 6577 of the transcript of the 4th of June, 2002 - you replied and described just the one occasion when Stojan Zupljanin came to Manjaca. I can read that to you, but I don't know whether the Prosecutor read this part of the transcript to you during proofing. But on those pages it says that you saw Stojan Zupljanin only once on that occasion and you only referred to him coming there only once. Do you remember your testimony in the Brdjanin case?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I do remember, but I have no reason to really pay attention to that. And so what am I supposed to do now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned -- after 17 years from the events, mentioned a possible second time that Stojan Zupljanin came to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: This is something that others told me. The inmates told me. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to quote what you said today on page 35 of the transcript. You did not prepare specifically to testify about this event, so there are mistakes or errors possible about that; isn't that correct? This is on transcript page 35, line 4, of today's transcript. So it's possible that then when you said in 2000 that your recollection was very fresh and that you said then what you actually remembered best, and that about the second time it's possible that you made a mistake?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: This is something that I heard from others. I didn't see him. Other inmates who talked about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Who talked with Stojan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember at the time when you were in Manjaca that a person by the name of Zarko Tole was with you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that is a Croatian --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mayor -- major or colonel?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: He was helping in the kitchen in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the president of the court from Sanski Most, Adil Draganovic, was there with you also; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And did Adil Draganovic perhaps tell you that he had spoken with Stojan Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell you. Adil comes from the same place as I do, so I would have told you right away that it was Adil who had told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Stojan Zupljanin and Adil Draganovic went to high school together?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that Stojan Zupljanin was a good friend with this Zarko Tole, the major from the Croatian Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that the reason he visited Manjaca was precisely to visit these two people and to talk with them?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, it's possible. He didn't talk to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Adil Draganovic testified in the Brdjanin case?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that in his testimony he said - and this is on transcript page 54/55 - that he saw Stojan Zupljanin once and that he spoke with him in Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Who said that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Adil Draganovic. Mr. Sabanovic, in the Brdjanin case, you spoke of the so-called TN [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: The police, territorial police?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Zupljanin, Kupresanin, and Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Because their names end in N?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I think there might need to be a correction to the transcript as well. Line 8 says "TN." I think my friend meant three N.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Three N.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the final letters of their last names; correct? Last names, I mean.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement and in your testimony, you call them politicians who held speeches; is that what you recall?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were politicians, security officers, and who knows what. And it wasn't my goal to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you gave the statement and the testimony in the Brdjanin case, you described them as politicians; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: That is probably all the same. In any case, they were the organisers. They must have been politicians and security officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you testified in the Brdjanin case, did you know what Stojan Zupljanin's position was?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: President of the Serb Republic of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You did not know that he was a policeman?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: He was president of the Serb Republic of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you believed he was a politician alongside the other two?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same thing for all three.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned the two visits, you mentioned the two visits by politicians, Kupresanin, Brdjanin, and Zupljanin; you through all of them in; they were all the same to you?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same, I didn't pay much heed to that; I expected nothing good to come out of it. And it didn't concern me in any negative way anyhow.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to approach the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After those events and prior to this testimony, did you have occasion to discuss these visits with Adil Draganovic?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in The Hague, it was then that you were asked about whether Stojan Zupljanin visited the camp once or twice for the first time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you were told that he visited Manjaca twice, and you accepted that?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Who told you that, the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. What sort of questions are these?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of proofing with the Prosecution, were you offered to sign the information you provided?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I have in mind the last few days.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not sign anything recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show P62 to the witness. I apologise, this is in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In any case, this is the proofing notes of a meeting you had with the Prosecution. Did they ask you to sign it afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know if anyone asked me to do so, and I don't remember signing anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I'm not sure where we are going with this. Either you attach some importance to the fact that your client did visit Manjaca once or maybe twice, and if that is the case, I would like you to assist the Court in explaining why this is important. Or you are testing the witness's credibility, which is perfectly legitimate, but I think the witness has answered the best he could on the issue of whether he actually saw Mr. Zupljanin once or twice at Manjaca. So could you clarify which direction we are going with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is two pronged. And at this stage I don't want to challenge the credibility of the witness. I'm merely seeking to point out that his recollection differs from the time when he gave his first statement, that it was far better then. And given that he was not proofed specifically for this event, that mistakes may have occurred. I'm trying to suggest to him that he mixed up the three N's including my client among the politicians who visited twice, because he mentioned all those politicians visiting twice. He did so in his previous testimony, it was only my client that was mentioned as visiting once. And all of a sudden now we have my client visiting twice. This is my position regarding that issue. As for the proofing notes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But why is it important whether your client visited once or twice?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My client was there in his private capacity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And there was nothing important about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the witness said, there was nothing important to it, so I didn't want to put too much focus on that. He was here in his private capacity to visit the two people I mentioned a moment ago, Adil Draganovic and Zarko Tole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Now you confuse me. Because if I understood it correctly, your client actually did address the detainees, and they applauded him, or was that not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only two of them individually in the presence of the commander. Adil Draganovic testified to that, and he will appear before this Chamber to speak about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So is it your point that your client -- your client never came to Manjaca in any official capacity?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This clarifies the issue. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if I could just mention the fact that I can't find in the Brdjanin transcript, and I wonder if my learned friend can help me with this, where it's stated by this witness that these three politicians came twice. He mentioned that all these politicians visited twice, and it's -- the portion of the transcript eludes me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bear with me. I'm looking for the reference for Talic twice. It's page 6688, and in the cross-examination of Mr. Ackerman there's a mention of Mr. Kupresanin. It is mentioned on several occasions in the transcript. Brdjanin, Talic, and Kupresanin; they all visited twice, alledgedly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once or five times is unimportant. What is important is what was taking place and why. It's not an issue if someone was there once or five times. For me it's irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Why don't you take it directly to the witness to simply settle the matter and put the question to the witness whether actually he is sure that he saw Mr. Zupljanin enter one of the stables and while he was in there he gave a speech to the detainees who then applauded him. This seems to be the crucial point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, you said at the beginning of your testimony that you saw Mr. Zupljanin outside the barracks, that he didn't enter your building, that you saw him outside?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: He couldn't enter my building because I was not in the barracks, I was not in the stable. I arrived later when he was already there, and I was not allowed to go in as he was moving from the second to the third stable. That's when I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You saw him outside?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for the umpteenth time. I do not understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As you saw him, did he talk to anyone?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't follow. I didn't dare, and I wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that was the sole time you saw him as Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard the rest from the stories going around, but I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, did you see Mr. Stojan Zupljanin enter into one of the stables?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw him come out of one building and -- as he moved toward the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And did you see him enter the other building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't look. I didn't care to look. The police were there and all that. And this was no marketplace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So your testimony is that you saw Mr. Zupljanin come out from one of the stables; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw him leave one stable building. I didn't say he entered the next one or anything of the sort. I didn't dare look. My life was in danger, and I didn't care to look who went where. What's this all about? Whether someone was there once or several times. He didn't hurt me, but all of them who came had the same goal. It was their task. They had their respective duties, and they performed them in the same way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, if you have followed the discussion, the issue that has arisen - and I'm sorry for taking over this - is whether Mr. Stojan Zupljanin visited Manjaca in his official capacity as head of the police in Banja Luka. He may -- please, Mr. Witness, hear me out. He may have visited the Manjaca camp in a purely private capacity because he wanted to meet up with somebody he knew there, yet he might also have visited the camp in his official capacity, in which case it is relevant for the Chamber to know whether during his visit he addressed some of the detainees. This is the issue. It's not whether he visited Manjaca once or twice. The issue is: When he visited, did he address the detainees in a speech. Now, you said that you were not in the building but you saw him come out and you also testified that you -- while he was in there, you heard the detainees applaud.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Is this your testimony today, that you heard him -- that you heard the detainees applaud him while he was in there and then you saw him come out from that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When he left the building. The applauding happened before, not when he was already outside. I'm surprised by this behaviour, that I'm now being asked whether he was there in his official capacity as if I was a manager or director there. And then as if I could tell you if he was there privately or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we are not expecting you to have an opinion about whether he was there in one or the other capacity. The only thing we are interested in is to hear what you observed and what you saw and what you heard. That is the only thing that we are asking you to give to us. And then we will make the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have said already, and I'm surprised that I'm being asked one in the same thing over and over again. I saw him when he came out, but I didn't see him enter another building or at the time of the applause inside. This is such a blamage. I have never seen this before. I saw lots of things but nothing anything like this. This is the truth. I don't know why he came privately or officially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you very much. I think this concludes the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabanovic, one last question on a different topic. Have a look at your statement. Page 10, the last paragraph. In that paragraph, which spills over to the next page, you describe how a lawyer came to see you telling you that he was a JNA investigator. Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: He was there, the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And he told you that in Sanski Most an indictment was issued against you? This is what it says; you can read it for yourself.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have to read it. I spent several hours writing a statement but what is in there is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And on the next page it says that he told you that the third count in the indictment was that: "I plotted against the Serb people by issuing certificates which" --

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: That is a lie. I can no longer keep this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is in your statement, that he told you.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Somebody type wrote this. I wrote on paper with a pencil.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You yourself described this event.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say this to anyone. I hear this for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is the statement given by you received from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what it's all about. I never said so, and I never heard this from anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So the entire statement is incorrect or just that part?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe this part, maybe all of this. I didn't read all of it, but this part is incorrect, that I said that I transgressed against the Serb people. There was a Serb woman and a child and two of mine even have no Muslim names, Ernest, Oliver, and Alan, so who is what? Who is prettier than the other? And see what you are using.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did the investigating magistrate ask you anything about these medical certificates?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: This was no magistrate. He was an interrogator.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In any case, did he ask you about it?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: About what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: About the medical certificates.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Not a word, he told me to sit and write about what I know. He asked me of Faik Biscevic who had recently passed away. He was also in Manjaca and his two sons were killed. He asked me to write about that. I used a pencil and I did so. And this one didn't even come to see me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So this part of your statement is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: It is incorrect, and this is not my statement. I've never heard of this. You are quite a disagreeable people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Perhaps we could clarify exactly which part of the statement we are talking about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 11, paragraph 1, in the B/C/S. Please bear with me, I'll tell you where it is in the English version. Page 10 in the English. The last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So in principle, the statement before you is not what you told the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: This was not what I said. This was not copied. I wrote in pencil and handed it over. It was some -- at some 2.00 a.m. I finished it, got in, and handed it over to him. We didn't exchange a word. He didn't ask me about anyone, and he no longer mentioned Faik Biscevic. As for what you are saying, no one asked me about this ever, and I've never said anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you never mentioned that topic to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if I did. If they asked me, I may have. I wasn't there to volunteer information.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I think the witness might be at cross purposes. Your Honours, the statement that my learned friend is asking him to comment on, my understanding is the statement he made to the Office of the Prosecutor. I think the witness may have confused the issue because he made a prior statement to some other authorities that were interrogating him. Perhaps my friend could clarify that for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the part I read out from the statement is something that you told the Prosecutor when describing that particular event and your encounter with the interrogator, this description of yours in the statement.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: The portion you mentioned is something I wasn't aware of, and I can't believe someone could put this together so nicely. Where is the inspiration from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So that part of the statement is not what you told the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I never said anything of the sort. I don't want to discuss this anymore. You are younger than me, and I'm still surprised by your behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I would just like to clarify, sir, going on from my learned friend's questioning which he has just finished, the portion of the statement that he was asking you to consider, page 10, the last paragraph of the English version of your statement dated the 1st and 2nd of December, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I wonder if we could have -- someone could assist me with the relevant B/C/S portion and have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's the last paragraph on page number 10 and the first paragraph on page number 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: That is of the B/C/S? And that's the English as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to read to you the relevant paragraph, page 10, the last paragraph from the statement: "The following day the investigator told me that I would be brought to the military court and liquidated once the war was over. This was also the first day that I had to examine all prisoners coming to the camp. The MPs came again and said I had to note all the injuries of the new prisoners. Among the new arrivals that day, there were 15 to 20 who were from Sanski Most." Perhaps if we could pause there and if you could confirm whether you agree with the contents of that portion of your statement.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I was constantly being threatened of being liquidated, but never in such words as I find here. I was frequently threatened. I will never forget that the policeman at 1.00 in the morning told me that they had checked the people from Kotor Varos and at 12.30 or 1.00 a.m. he told me that the next day I would be butchered. Luckily for me, he was transferred to Gradacac. That's what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And you recall speaking with the investigator, who was mentioned in this paragraph of your statement?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: I did talk but about nothing much. And as for this that I said that he asked me about an inmate who was there, his name was Faik Biscevic, it was nothing particular. He went outside, and I was sitting there writing down with a pencil who was doing what, but I don't know that he talked with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: The balance of that paragraph in your statement, and I'm, with Your Honours's position going to summarise, talks about a person coming to Manjaca who was a former policeman in Sanski Most who you knew and you examined and who subsequently died. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: He came when he was well. I know that there was a police officer in that group in July when 19 or 21 dead people were brought in, so I saw them in the truck, in the transporter who were taken back. Josip Mlinar was there; he was dead. I don't know that he told me anything, because he was dead. And as for this inspector, I don't know. I mean, that wasn't then, and this person wasn't dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: The next paragraph of your statement, which my friend was asking you about, top of page 11 talks about you signing the death certificate.

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: This is not my statement. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall being interviewed by members of the Office of the Prosecutor in -- on the 1st and 2nd of December, 2001; and the 14th, 17th, and 19th February -- 2000; and the 14th, 17th, and 19th of February, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: Probably I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And do you recall being given the opportunity to read the statement in a language that you understand and then signing the statement in the presence of a third person; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ENIS SABANOVIC
utterances.text: This is not my statement. Perhaps there are parts which are, but this is not my statement. I didn't say that I had done something wrong against the Serbian people, that I had issued false permits. I'm not a bad person. And, I mean, I don't know what is the logic? That investigator was quite correct. He gave me a piece of paper and a pencil and I was writing on it, and then I gave it back to him. I don't know who did what to that later, who wrote on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, just for interruption. So, just for the record, Your Honours, that ERN number is 0200-4435 was completely denied by this witness, just for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm not sure that's an accurate reflection of the evidence that's come out, and I'm seeking to clarify this at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, at what point would he have completely denied it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's what just he said, so I just want to be a recorded this, that the statement dated 1st, 2nd December, 2000; and 14, 17, 19 February, 2001, was not his statement. Simply as that, Your Honour. Just for the record. Because he just stated it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You mean he has only just stated that, not on some previous occasion?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, this one. This statement that's in front of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, it's late. The witness is probably tired as we all are, concentration tends to wain. But generally, you are re-examining your witness. And correct me, but isn't this document already in as an exhibit? So I am not sure I see the path that you are taking with re-examining him on what I suppose, according to your case, is a previous consistent statement. How does it assist the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, to clarify, this statement is not an exhibit. The exhibit that's tendered for this witness is his prior testimony in the Brdjanin case. Your Honours don't have the benefit of having this as informal evidence. My concern is that a bald statement by my learned friend Mr. Pantelic that he has completely changed his story, so to speak, which, I think, is what he's wanting you to take away from this is not a true representation of what has come from this witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Can you say assist me. How do we get to this in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Because the last line of questioning from Mr. Pantelic's team was about the last paragraph in page 11 of this statement where it was purportedly a comment by my -- by the witness that he was -- that he took issue with. And in explaining that, he seems to have, it seems to have expanded to him dismissing the entire statement. I'm happy to leave it there, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I was about to say that. The point we are at is asked and answered. Can you take it any further?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Because the statement is not part of the evidence, and the evidence is his prior statement in the Brdjanin case, I'm happy to leave it there, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I only have one other area that I want to cover with this witness in re-examination, and that is, you were asked, sir, in cross-examination about the guards at the detention facility or the hall, sports hall, Hasan Kikic and you described them as military police. Now, could you please explain to the Chamber what you mean by that term?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I know is that it's called the military police. I'm not a military person. I don't follow anything about the army or the military. All I know is that whoever entered of them, they said they were in the military police. As for the uniforms, whether they wore this or that uniform, it wasn't some kind of already established Serbian Republic of Krajina, but that's what they were fighting for. There were no problems, it was just one army fighting the two other people who were victims of that. All they asked me was -- I mean, asking me whether this colour of uniform or that colour of uniform, is this a military police or not, everybody then was wearing some kind of military uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, nobody is asking you whether this colour or that colour, is that kind of uniform or that kind of uniform. The only thing that you could have observed is the colour of the uniform. In that gym, was it a blue one or was it not a blue one, or don't you know? That's the only thing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to say that I wasn't interested. I wasn't allowed to look at people. What sort of a colour are you wearing? Are you coming here for a feast? Are you getting married? I cannot understand the way you are behaving towards me. I simply hate hate, and lies.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I have no further questions, thank you, sirs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, thank you for attending. It's been a long day. We thank you for your assistance, and we wish you a safe journey back to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't difficult for me. I am not tired. I don't feel sorry, but thank you. We really need to stick to what sort of a situation it was. Perhaps there was some misstatements and mistakes in speech, but I apologise. Nobody insulted me today either, but I'm just not capable of listening to anything. But thank you all of you here, I wish you much luck in your further work and investigations. I'm losing when I'm coming here. I work. So when I'm not working, I lose out. I am privately employed. I work in a private clinic. Every day that I miss work, I lose 300 Euros. But I'm not sorry about that, it's just that I'm sorry if I come and hear something here that was not. But thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. You are released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, in the six minutes remaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Can we deal with your administrative issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It concerns scheduling regarding the Prosecution's proposed expert witness Ms. Hanson, expert on Crisis Staffs. There was some recent disclosure of a transcript of testimony that she made in the state court proceeding in Bosnia in January of this year, and in light of that, we thought there would be some opposition from the Defence about the timing of her appearance. I think I'm stating it correctly, my understanding is that they are agreeable with her attending Friday for direct examination, but then they would ask that her cross-examination be put off until later the following week after we've done the videolink witness that's scheduled. And I think he was currently scheduled for Tuesday, we'd like to move him up to Monday, if that's possible. And do him on Monday and Tuesday and have Ms. Hanson follow that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: If that's possible, that's fine. Does the Defence agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand the Defence agrees and the Registry has confirmed that it's technically possible. So we'll proceed thus.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before we take the adjournment, is there anything else? Thank you. We resume tomorrow afternoon at 2.15 in Courtroom I. I am given to understand that there may be a change on Thursday, but by tomorrow's adjournment, the Chamber would certainly be in a position to confirm to you at what time on Thursday and Friday we will resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
